Govt relaxes guidelines under Export Promotion Mission to help MSME exporters reach new markets
 So far, a total of 11 interventions under two sub-schemes of the Export Promotion Mission have been operationalised
 Updated - November 18, 2026 10:03 pm IST - New Delhi 
 The Hindu Bureau READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 For illustration
 The Ministry of Commerce and Industry on Wednesday amended various guidelines in its Export Promotion Mission (EMP) with the aim of further empowering exporters to expand into new markets, create awareness about their products, helping them meet international standards, and addressing logistical gaps within India.
 The amendments have been made to three interventions under the Niryat Disha sub-scheme of the EPM. The Union Cabinet had approved the EPM on November 12, 2025, with an outlay of ₹25,060 crore for the period 2025-26 to 2030-31.
 Helping exporter create awareness
 One of these, the Market Access Support (MAS) intervention, is aimed at providing structured support to exporters for activities such as Buyer-Seller Meets (BSMs), Reverse Buyer-Seller Meets (RBSMs), trade fairs, exhibitions and other related market access initiatives.
 MSMEs seek curbs on steel, metal price surge; urge Centre to cut import duties Under the amended guidelines, the maximum eligible export turnover for availing airfare reimbursement for participation in BSMs, trade fairs and trade delegations has been increased from ₹75 lakh to ₹50 crore.
 Further, the airfare reimbursement has been enhanced to up to 95% for micro and small exporters and up to 80% for other eligible exporters. The mandatory membership period with Export Promotion Councils has also been reduced from six months to three months.
 Meeting international standards
 The Trade Regulations, Accreditation & Compliance Enablement (TRACE) intervention is aimed at helping micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in meeting international quality, safety, and technical requirements.
 “Under the amended guidelines, the list of certificates eligible for reimbursement has been expanded from 462 to 600, enabling wider coverage and greater support for MSMEs in meeting international quality, safety and technical requirements,” the government said in a release.
 Lok Sabha passes MSME Development Amendment Bill without debate Overcoming logistical challenges
 The Logistics Interventions for Freight and Transport (LIFT) intervention is aimed at addressing geographical disadvantages and logistics gaps faced by MSMEs in low export-intensity areas.
 The amended guidelines expand the coverage of low export-intensity districts from 13 States and Union Territories (UTs) to 34 States and UTs.
 The categories of eligible ports have been widened to include Land Customs Stations (LCSs) and Integrated Check Posts (ICPs) and waterways have been added to the existing modes of transport: road, rail, and air.
 The new guidelines also now extend air freight support for export shipments from Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh, in addition to the existing coverage of the North Eastern region.
 The minimum distance eligibility criterion between the origin and destination ports has been reduced from 200 km to 100 km, and support under this mechanism has been extended to all exportable merchandise items, except those specified in a negative list.
